entries.input: Let $f$ be twice differentiable on $[a, b]$ with $f(a) < 0 < f(b)$, $f' \geq \delta > 0$ and $0 \leq f'' \leq M$ there, and let $\xi \in (a, b)$ be the zero of $f$. If $x_1 \in (\xi, b)$ and $x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n)$, then $x_n \to \xi$.
entries.name: NewtonMethodConverges
entries.binders: (f : ℝ → ℝ) (a b δ M ξ : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hd2 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, DifferentiableAt ℝ (deriv f) x) (hfa : f a < 0) (hfb : 0 < f b) (hδ : 0 < δ) (h1 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, δ ≤ deriv f x) (h2 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, 0 ≤ deriv (deriv f) x ∧ deriv (deriv f) x ≤ M) (hξ : ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b) (hξ0 : f ξ = 0) (x : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : x 0 ∈ Set.Ioo ξ b) (hx : ∀ n, x (n + 1) = x n - f (x n) / deriv f (x n))
entries.title: Newton's method
entries.witness_note: Satisfiable: `f x = x` on `[-1, 1]` with `ξ = 0`, `δ = 1`, `M = 0` and the constant-zero sequence after one step; the hypotheses are routine but numerous, so no term is recorded.
